arcs.title: Dana: Haifa
arcs.stage: Mon: he asked her out for Saturday, she said yes, 'things change in January'. Wed: short with a supplier at lunch; Lior let slip she took Monday off 'up north'; at 18:30 she came up for leftover Minced Beef Pie and left early ('have a good trip'). Thu night: she texts 'something I should tell you, in person, nothing bad, maybe'. Next: first date Sat Nov 21 (walk, Avi's, then the PixelPlex horror film with her at 21:00); she almost tells him.
arcs.secret: Dana has been offered a job running a new cafe in Haifa from January and must answer by Mon Dec 7. She has not told Ishai.

arcs.title: Gadi: Unpaid
arcs.stage: Wed: the number moved to Sunday ('Ofer on reserve'); Gadi then pulled the coffee-shop logo to 'tomorrow' and Ishai sent a rough file at 22:17. Thu: Ruti emails Ishai directly (jobs without an agency, the whole app); he tells Gadi 'nobody called', tells him he pays late every time, saves 'can I think about it?' as a draft. Next: Sunday's number; he hasn't answered Ruti.
arcs.secret: Sababa Creative lost its biggest client in October. Gadi is paying every freelancer late and hides it behind cheerful 'small things'.

arcs.title: Noa: Shir
arcs.stage: Mon-Wed: the 'S.' box, two couch nights, 'S.: the keys are with the neighbour'. She slipped out at 3 a.m. Wed night, leaving her beanie; Thu text: 'plumbers done'. Thu night Ishai says he doesn't believe the plumbers (his improv homework); 'amazing' x3; Shabbat dinner Friday: maybe. Yael let slip Noa paid cash for the lessons. Next: Sat Nov 28 he finds out.
arcs.secret: Noa's girlfriend of three years, Shir, moved out in October. Noa told nobody: it's why she is late, cancels plans and pushes Ishai's love life so hard.

arcs.title: Improv on Thursdays
arcs.stage: Lesson 3 Thu Nov 19: the toaster refund; he stays after a no and says 'I want to be paid for what I already did'; can't say no himself. Homework: one no to someone he likes (he uses it on Noa's plumbers). Lesson 4 Thu Nov 26, the last one Noa paid for.

arcs.title: Mrs. Levi's cough
arcs.stage: Wed: Moti took her to the clinic. Thu: bronchitis, she stays home; Ishai feeds the cats every morning (warm, for Ben-Gurion); 'everybody has a word so nobody asks the next question'. He asked about Eli twice. Next: he quietly messages Eli (week 3).
arcs.secret: Mrs. Levi is lonely: her son Eli in Toronto hasn't visited in four years, and she always says he's busy.

arcs.title: Avi's kiosk
arcs.stage: Tue: no proverb, a lawyer's envelope. Thu: 'the proverbs are finished', 'I have a calculator'; Ishai asks about the envelope, no answer. Next: he asks properly (week 3).
arcs.secret: Avi's landlord is doubling the kiosk's rent from January.

arcs.title: Lior's novel and Moshe
arcs.stage: Mon: chapter twelve, 'she says yes'. Wed: chapter thirteen, 'the man buys a coat for a cold city he's never been to'; lets slip Dana took Monday off 'up north' and backpedals. Ishai still doesn't recognise himself.
arcs.secret: Lior's novel is about Ishai: 'the man who apologises to his coffee'.

arcs.title: Tomer and Noa
arcs.stage: Wed Nov 18: the Pump House gallery night (Quiet Signals) with Ishai; 'same time next week, I'm putting it in my calendar'. Next: the bar, showing up for Noa.
arcs.secret: Tomer has liked Noa since school.

arcs.title: Mr. Zelig's bench
arcs.stage: Sat: one true sentence for the photo; Dana sat on his bench Thursday 'looking at her phone like it was the sea... not this sea'. 1971: 'I stayed.'

arcs.title: The poker table
arcs.stage: Thu Nov 19: Boaz invites Ishai at Avi's ('we're one short, and you're quiet'), 50 to buy in; Ishai says yes without a sorry. First night Mon Nov 23 (engine). After it: Yossi asks Ishai to lend him 200.
arcs.secret: Yossi is broke: the lucky cap hasn't paid in months, and he owes money at the depot.

beats.goal: First morning of feeding Mrs. Levi's cats as promised to Moti. On the landing Ishai feeds Ben-Gurion; Mrs. Levi talks from her doorway, hoarse: the clinic said bronchitis, she calls it 'a little cold with a big name'. A text from Noa: she went home at 3, 'plumbers done', keep the beanie. Mrs. Levi: everybody has a word so nobody asks the next question (Eli is 'busy'). Ishai asks about Eli; she sends him back to his dog.
beats.teaser: Mrs. Levi's cough gets a big name, and Noa vanishes at 3
beats.forceText: Ishai feeds Mrs. Levi's cats on the landing; she croaks 'bronchitis' from her door and won't talk about Eli.

forceLines.say: The doctor says bronchitis. I say a little cold with a big name.
Every morning, Mrs. Levi. Cats first, then questions.

forceCommentary.say: Bronchitis. Week two said 'hold my tea'.
Ben-Gurion eats first. Even the cat knows the hierarchy.

moments.text: On the landing Ishai shakes dry food into a dish for Ben-Gurion the grey cat. Mrs. Levi's door opens a crack; she leans on the frame, wrapped up, her voice gone to a croak.

lines.say: You came. Ben-Gurion told me first, he doesn't wait quietly.
Morning, Mrs. Levi. You sound worse than yesterday.
The doctor says bronchitis. I say a little cold with a big name.
Bronchitis isn't a little cold. Are you taking what Moti brought?
Three times a day, like a prayer. Bitter like one too.
Do you need anything? Soup? Lemons? I can go to the market.
I need you to stop worrying. And the grey one likes it warm.
Warm cat food. Okay. A little water from the kettle.
See? You listen. Not everybody listens.
Did Eli call? About the clinic?

commentary.say: Her voice is gone and she still out-talks him. Respect.
Warm cat food. The cat has a better care plan than most people.

moments.text: Mrs. Levi looks away down the stairs. Ishai's phone buzzes in his pocket; he reads it on the landing, frowning.

lines.say: Noa. She left at three in the morning. 'The plumbers are done.'
At three in the morning? Plumbers? In this country?
That's what I said. In my head.
Eli is busy. Your Noa has plumbers. Everybody has a word.
What do you mean, a word?
A word you say so nobody asks the next question.
Then I'll ask the next question. Did Eli call?
Go, go, your dog is crying behind the door. Tomorrow again?
Every morning. I promised Moti. And you.
Then tomorrow I'll be better. For the cats.

commentary.say: 'Everybody has a word.' Write that on the building's front door.
He asked about Eli twice. She dodged twice. Tie game.

message.say: Went home at 3, couldn't sleep. Plumbers done, all fixed! Keep my beanie hostage. Love you, nerd.

update.memory: Bronchitis. Ishai fed the cats, warm, and asked about Eli twice. I told him everybody has a word. He comes every morning now.

beats.goal: At his desk Ishai finds an email from Ruti, the chickpea client, not through Sababa: she loves his work and asks if he takes jobs without an agency (the whole app). Then Gadi phones about last night's rough logo and wants colours. Ishai asks vaguely whether Ruti talks to other designers; Gadi: everything goes through Sababa. 'Did she call you?' 'Nobody called' (it was an email). Ishai holds: colours after Sunday's number. He saves a reply to Ruti as a draft. Phone only: Gadi is never seen.
beats.teaser: Ishai's inbox gets a message Gadi really wouldn't like
beats.forceText: Ruti emails Ishai directly asking if he works without an agency; he tells Gadi 'nobody called' and saves a draft reply.

forceLines.say: Ruti talks to me. Everything goes through Sababa, that's the beauty.
Colours after the number, Gadi. Like we said.

forceCommentary.say: Technically nobody called. She emailed. Lawyer Ishai has entered the chat.
Loyalty versus rent. Rent is undefeated.

moments.text: At his desk Ishai opens his email: a new message, not from Sababa but from Ruti, the chickpea client. He reads it twice, then out loud to Falafel.

lines.say: 'I love your work. Do you take jobs without an agency? We need the whole app. Ruti.'
Without an agency. Falafel, that means without Gadi.

commentary.say: The client went around the agency. That's the business version of a love letter.
Falafel has no opinion on agency fees. Yet.

moments.text: The phone rings on the desk while the email is still open. Gadi. Ishai minimises the window as if Gadi could see it.

lines.say: Ishai! I saw the file at midnight. You're a machine. A tired machine.
You said tomorrow, so I sent it tonight. It's rough.
Rough is good! Rough is honest! The client wants colours, though.
Gadi, does Ruti... does Ruti talk to other designers?
Ruti? Ruti talks to me. Everything goes through Sababa, that's the beauty.
Right. The beauty.
Why? Did she call you? She shouldn't call you. It confuses things.
No. Nobody called.
Good. Sunday, the number, colours by then, we settle it all together.
Colours after the number, Gadi. Like we said.

commentary.say: He minimised the window. Gadi is on the phone. That's not how screens work, babe.
'Nobody called.' Technically true. She emailed. Our boy found a loophole.

moments.text: Ishai stands by the window with the phone, one hand on the sill next to Moshe.

lines.say: Like we said, like we said. You sound like a lawyer now.
I sound like a person with rent on the first.
Everybody has rent! I have rent! Ofer has rent, on reserve duty!
Then everybody understands why I'd like to be paid.
My favourite pixel. Have I ever not paid you?
Late. You've paid me late. Every time this year.
Late is a kind of on time. Sunday. Promise. Love to the basil.
Moshe says Sunday too. Bye, Gadi.

commentary.say: 'Late is a kind of on time.' Put it on Sababa's business cards.
'Every time this year.' He said it out loud. I need to sit down.

update.memory: Ishai sent a rough logo at midnight, wants colours only after Sunday's number. Told me I pay late. Asked oddly about Ruti; said nobody called.

moments.text: Ishai opens Ruti's email again, types a long reply, deletes it, types one line, and saves it as a draft.

lines.say: 'Thank you. Can I think about it?' Draft. Coward's draft.

commentary.say: A draft is a yes wearing a hoodie.
Saved, not sent. The most Ishai button on the keyboard.

beats.goal: Lunch on Herzl Street. Boaz, in his 88 bus driver's shirt, eats falafel at Avi's on his break and invites Ishai to poker at his place Monday at 20:00 ('we're one short, and you're quiet'): 50 shekels to buy in, pizza, Moti, Ronit the maths teacher, Yossi and his lucky cap. Ishai says yes without saying sorry. Then Avi serves him with no proverb, the lawyer's envelope in his apron; Ishai asks, Avi deflects ('proverbs are for people with time').
beats.teaser: Boaz needs a fourth player, and Avi's proverbs are gone
beats.forceText: Boaz invites Ishai to Monday poker ('we're one short, and you're quiet'); Ishai says yes. Avi serves him with no proverb.

forceLines.say: Monday, eight, poker at my place. We're one short, and you're quiet.
Yes. I'll come. No sorry. Just yes.

forceCommentary.say: Poker. Ishai. The man who apologises to vending machines.
Quiet is good at a table. Quiet is also good at losing.

moments.text: At Avi's kiosk Boaz, in his bus driver's shirt, eats a falafel standing up on his break. He waves Ishai over with the half pita.

lines.say: Ishai! The quiet one. Come, stand, Avi's sauce is better with company.
Boaz. Aren't you supposed to be driving the 88?
Twenty minutes' break. The 88 knows the way without me.
Thanks again for coming to the film on Saturday.
A Doll's House. She was right to leave. Don't tell Ronit I said that.
Who's Ronit?
Exactly why I was looking for you. Monday night, poker, at my place.
Poker? Me? I don't really know how to...
We're one short, and you're quiet. Quiet is good at a table.
Quiet is also good at losing.

commentary.say: Boaz recruiting at the falafel stand. This is how gangs start, Oren.
A bus driver's break: twenty minutes, one falafel, one new victim.

moments.text: Boaz wipes his hands on a napkin and counts the details off on his fingers.

lines.say: Fifty shekels buys you in. Pizza's on me. Monday, eight.
Who else plays?
Moti from apartment one, he counts everything. Ronit, she teaches maths.
A committee head and a maths teacher. Wonderful.
And Yossi from the depot. Lucky cap. Don't touch the cap.
I won't touch the cap.
So? Yes? Don't say sorry, just say yes.
Yes. I'll come. Monday at eight.
Good. Ronit will read you like a timetable. Bring small notes.
Small notes. Don't touch the cap. Got it.

commentary.say: A maths teacher at the table. His chances just got a decimal point.
He said yes with zero sorries. Somebody frame that.

update.memory: Invited Ishai to Monday poker, fifty to buy in. He said yes without a sorry. Warned him about Ronit and Yossi's cap.

moments.text: Boaz hurries back to his bus. At the kiosk Avi wraps Ishai's falafel in silence, the lawyer's envelope sticking out of his apron pocket again.

lines.say: One falafel, Avi. And today's proverb, please.
Today there's tahini. The proverbs are finished.
Finished? You've had one every day for three years.
Proverbs are for people with time. I have a calculator.
Is it the envelope? I saw it on Tuesday too.
You see a lot for a man who apologises to pita.
Sorry. I mean, I'm not sorry. I'm asking.
Eat. It's hot. Hot things don't wait.
That sounded like a proverb.
It was a fact. Twelve shekels.

commentary.say: No proverb, an envelope, a calculator. Avi, blink twice.
'It was a fact. Twelve shekels.' The coldest receipt on Herzl Street.

update.memory: Ishai asked about the envelope. No proverb, no answer. He noticed. He keeps noticing.

beats.goal: Improv lesson 3 with Yael at the back of The Black Candle: hearing no and staying in the scene. Ishai returns a toaster that burns everything; he leaves at the first 'no', then stays ('yes, and I'm still standing here'), asks for the policy 'with a date, because Sunday keeps moving', and says out loud 'I want to be paid for what I already did.' Then the swap: he must say no and can't. Homework: say no once to someone you like. After class on the street Yael mentions Noa paid for the four lessons in cash.
beats.teaser: Improv lesson three: someone says no, and Ishai has to stay
beats.forceText: Improv lesson 3: Ishai learns to stay in a scene after a no, and says 'I want to be paid for what I already did.'

forceLines.say: In life a no ends the scene. Here it's just the next line.
I want to be paid for what I already did!

forceCommentary.say: A toaster, a refund and a breakthrough. Thursday delivers.
Homework: say no to someone you like. Hardest assignment in Tel Aviv.

moments.text: The back room of The Black Candle, tables pushed to the walls, the class in a half circle of chairs. Yael claps once and calls Ishai to the cleared floor first.

lines.say: Lesson three. Today someone says no to you, and you stay in the scene.
Can I stay in the chair instead?
No. See? Already a no. And you're standing. Good.
I'm standing because you looked at me.
You're a customer, I'm a shop. You want your money back.
Hi. Sorry. I bought this toaster. It's a very nice toaster.
Then why are you returning it?
It burns everything. Sorry. Toast, mostly. A napkin once.
No refunds. Store policy.
Oh. Okay. Sorry to bother you. Have a nice—

commentary.say: He apologised to a toaster he invented. Character work.
One 'no' and he was out the door. Personal best: zero seconds.

moments.text: Yael stops the scene with a raised hand. The class laughs; Ishai walks back onto the floor and tries again, standing a little straighter.

lines.say: Stop. You left. I said no and you left the shop.
That's what you do when someone says no.
In life, maybe. Here a no is just the next line. Again.
Hi. This toaster burns everything. I want my money back.
No refunds. Store policy.
Yes, and I'm still standing here with a burnt napkin.
Ha. Good. And?
And I'd like to see the policy. Written down. With a date.
Why a date?
Because Sunday keeps moving. I mean, store policies move.

commentary.say: 'Sunday keeps moving.' That's not about a toaster, Zohar.
Gadi, if you're watching, the toaster is you.

moments.text: Yael steps closer and lowers her voice, still in the scene. The half circle goes quiet.

lines.say: Who keeps moving Sunday, Ishai? Don't answer me. Answer the shop.
You do. You say it's all coming together. It's never together.
Good. Now say what you want. One sentence. No sorry.
I want... I want to be paid for what I already did.
Louder. The shop is old and the shop is deaf.
I want to be paid for what I already did!
Everyone, that's it. That's the whole lesson. Sit, before you apologise.
I wasn't going to apolo... okay, I was.

commentary.say: He yelled. Our Ishai yelled. At a fake shop, but still.
The class applauded a refund request. Tel Aviv in one picture.

moments.text: Yael swaps the roles: now Ishai is the shop and she is the customer. He stands behind an imaginary counter and keeps wanting to hand over the money.

lines.say: Swap. Now you're the shop. I want a refund, and you say no.
Of course, here's your money. Sorry about the toaster.
Ishai. You just gave away the whole shop.
It's a very small shop.
Try once. 'No.' Two letters. Nobody dies.
No. Hm. No... but I could fix your toaster.
That's a no with a yes, and. I'll take it.
It felt terrible. Like stepping on a cat.
Homework: say no once this week, to someone you like.
Someone I like? That's the worst homework you've ever given.

commentary.say: Asking for money: unlocked. Saying no: still loading.
'Someone you like.' Dana, Noa, Gadi... who gets the no?

moments.text: Outside on Herzl Street after class, Yael zips her coat and walks with Ishai toward the bus stop.

lines.say: Next week is the last of the four Noa paid for. Then it's your money.
Noa paid for them? She told me it was a gift voucher.
A voucher she paid for. In cash. Quite a lot, actually.
She's been very generous lately. Very... everything.
Generous people need a no sometimes too. Remember that.
Is that part of the homework?
That's the bonus question. See you Thursday, Ishai.
See you Thursday. Thank you. Not sorry. Thank you.

commentary.say: Noa paid cash. For his lessons. While her pipes 'got fixed'. Hmm.
'Not sorry. Thank you.' Lesson three, passed with a limp.

update.memory: Lesson 3: he said 'I want to be paid for what I already did' out loud. Saying no is still agony. Homework: one no to someone he likes.

beats.goal: At home in the evening, Noa's wool beanie in his hand, Ishai phones Noa. He does his homework: 'no, I don't believe the plumbers came at three in the morning.' She says 'amazing' three times, she's just tired; he invites her for Shabbat dinner Friday, no questions; she says maybe. She teases him about Saturday (walk, Avi's, then the horror film with Dana). After he hangs up, a text from Dana: Saturday still on? Something she should tell him, in person, 'nothing bad, maybe'.
beats.teaser: Noa gets Ishai's first 'no', then Dana sends a strange text
beats.forceText: Ishai tells Noa he doesn't believe the plumbers story; she deflects. Then Dana texts: something to tell him Saturday, in person.

forceLines.say: No. I don't believe the plumbers came at three in the morning.
Everything is amazing. The pipes are amazing. I'm amazing.

forceCommentary.say: Homework done. He said no to Noa. I'm so proud I could cry.
Three amazings. That's two more than a fine person needs.

moments.text: Ishai sits in the armchair with Noa's wool beanie in his hand and calls her. She answers on the fifth ring, somewhere very quiet.

lines.say: Hi. I have your beanie. It's being held hostage, as instructed.
Good. Keep it warm. How was Yael? Did you say no to anyone?
The homework is to say no to someone I like. So, no.
No what?
No, I don't believe the plumbers came at three in the morning.
Ishush. Wow. Look at you. Lesson three really worked.
Noa. Is everything okay? At your place?
Everything is amazing. The pipes are amazing. I'm amazing.
That's three amazings. You told me three sorries max.
Okay, smart guy. I'm tired, that's all. Busy month.

commentary.say: He used the homework on Noa. Within four hours. Overachiever.
'Somewhere very quiet.' Her flat is never quiet. Noted.

moments.text: Ishai gets up and walks to the window, the beanie still in his hand, talking softer now.

lines.say: You can sleep here again. The armchair misses you.
The armchair is a liar. My back says hello, by the way.
Then come Friday for Shabbat dinner. Candles, soup, no questions.
No questions? You? You just asked four.
Starting Friday. No questions. Promise.
Maybe. I'll text you. Now go plan Saturday, Mister Date.
Saturday is planned. A walk, Avi's, then the film.
A horror film on a first date. Bold. She'll grab your arm.
Or she'll leave at the intermission.
She won't. Good night, Ishush. Thanks for keeping the hostage.

commentary.say: A horror film on a first date. Either brilliant or a documentary.
'Maybe' to Shabbat dinner. Noa never says maybe to soup.

update.memory: Ishai didn't buy my plumbers, for homework. I said amazing three times. He invited me Friday, no questions. I said maybe.

moments.text: He hangs up and puts the beanie on the shelf by the door. The phone buzzes again: Dana. He reads it standing still in the middle of the room.

lines.say: 'Nothing bad. Maybe.' Who puts a maybe after nothing bad?
Okay. Reply. 'Still on.' Not sorry. Just... still on.

commentary.say: 'Nothing bad, maybe.' Translation: very something, definitely.
Two women, two messages, zero straight answers. It's Thursday.

message.say: Saturday still on? There's something I should tell you. In person. Nothing bad. Maybe. Good night, Ishai.

hook.text: Dana texts: 'There's something I should tell you. In person. Nothing bad. Maybe.' What does Dana need to tell him on Saturday?

previously.text: Noa fell asleep mid-sentence; her phone read 'S.: the keys are with the neighbour'. He turned it face down. By bedtime the armchair was empty, only her beanie left behind.

hosts: Thursday. Cats at eight, improv at five. Two things Ishai can't say no to.
Noa left at three in the morning. Plumbers, apparently. Night-shift plumbers.
Mrs. Levi's cough has a name now. A long one. She hates it.
Ben-Gurion the cat eats before anyone else in that building. As he should.
Somewhere in Ishai's inbox there's a message he hasn't answered. I can feel it.
Gadi's favourite word is Sunday. His second favourite is together.
Rent is due on the first. Gadi's Sunday is due... eventually.
Boaz drives the 88 all day and still walks everywhere. Respect.
Poker at Boaz's on Monday. Somebody teach Ishai what a poker face is.
Avi used to give a proverb with every falafel. Count today's proverbs. I'll wait.
A lawyer's envelope in an apron pocket. That's not a menu.
Improv lesson three tonight. Last week was 'I want'. Guess what's next.
Yael could make a lamp post say what it wants. Ishai is harder than a lamp post.
Saturday: a walk, Avi's, then a horror film. Romance, Tel Aviv style.
Dana drew a basil leaf every day this week. Some days smaller. I'm just saying.
Lior asked if anyone knows the trains to the north. For research. Of course.
Moshe the basil had a good week. He's the only one.
Falafel the dog has a better sleep schedule than everyone in this building.
Kobi bought a new lottery notebook. The old one is 'retired with honours'.
Mr. Zelig fed the pigeons in alphabetical order today. Don't ask how.
Fifteen degrees and partly cloudy. Jacket weather. Ishai owns one jacket.
Noa's beanie is on Ishai's shelf. Some hats travel. Some hats wait.
Moti counts the committee money twice. Monday he counts chips.
Tomer is already planning next Wednesday. He's never planned anything.
Somebody in this show is hiding something. Pick a name. Any name.
Thursday rule: if it's quiet at the café, Lior is writing about you.
radio: Radio Herzl 88.2, good morning to everyone up early on purpose.
Fifteen degrees and some clouds. Your jacket called. It misses you.
Thursday in Tel Aviv: the weekend is close enough to smell.
A listener asks how to say no politely. Short answer: no. Long answer: no, thank you.
Traffic on the coastal road. The sea is not moving either.
If your plumber comes at three in the morning, call us. We have questions.
Shuk Shalom says the clementines are in. Season of sticky fingers.
It's a good evening to call someone you haven't called. Not your boss.
Tip from the studio: a draft is not an answer. Hit send or hit delete.
Herzl Street at dusk. Buses, bikes and one very confident pigeon.
Tomorrow is Friday. Candles at four eighteen. Start the soup now.
Radio Herzl 88.2. Stay warm, stay kind, and keep your receipts.

zelig: The pigeons know who's leaving. They always know.
A no is a door. A yes is a window. I prefer windows.
In 1971 I said no once. Then I bought pigeons.
Thursday is for listening. Friday for talking.
michal: Run club tomorrow at seven. I will be there in spirit.
Mirror, tell me the truth. No, don't.
Squats are just sitting with ambition.
sivan: Six kilometres before work. Some people call that a warm-up.
The guy with the dog walked. Again.
Level eight. Not seven. Never seven.
lior: Chapter fourteen: the man learns a new word. The word is no.
Trains to the north leave every half hour. For research.
He apologised to a toaster. No, too much. Keep it.
She stood at the window again. I wrote it down. I always write it down.
A coat for a cold city. Still the best line I have.
kobi: Thursday numbers are lucky numbers. Ask anyone. Ask me.
New notebook. Same system. The system is perfect.
One more, then I'm a responsible adult.
Lottery's Saturday. I'm already rich on paper.

street: ...he said Sunday, and I said which Sunday...
...three in the morning? who calls a plumber at three...
market: ...clementines, two for ten, the good ones...
...she wanted the whole recipe, I gave her half...
park: ...the old man named the pigeons again...
...I'm not running, I'm jogging with intention...
...the duck has a better life than me...
cafe: ...the barista's off on Monday, someone said up north...
...oat milk, if there is any oat milk...
...he's writing again, the man by the window...

chat.say: Mrs. Levi is resting at home. Please knock softly. The cats are being fed. Moti
Who left a beanie on the stairs? Oh wait, it's gone. Never mind.
Committee fees: three apartments still missing. You know who you are.
Thank you for the soup, whoever. I am fine. A little cold with a big name.
Monday evening there will be some noise from apt 2. Cards. Not a party. Mostly cards.
Is anyone else's hot water lukewarm or is it a personal message?
Hot water: the boiler man comes Sunday. Daytime. Not three in the morning.
Good night everyone. Close the stair window, the cats get ideas.
